pl-l4d12c5-d1e115.summary: Asks whether what the priest does is properly called sacrifice or immolation, and whether Christ is immolated daily or was immolated only once.

pl-l4d12c5-d1e118.summary: Answers briefly that what the priest offers and consecrates is called a sacrifice and offering because it is a memorial and representation of the true sacrifice and holy immolation made on the altar of the cross. Christ died once, on the cross, and was immolated there in himself; he is immolated daily in the sacrament, because in the sacrament what was done once is remembered.
claims: The eucharist is a sacrifice as memorial and representation of the cross.
Christ was immolated once in himself and is immolated daily in the sacrament.

pl-l4d12c5-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: we know Christ rising from the dead dies no more; yet lest we forget what was done once, it is done in our memory each year at Easter. Is Christ killed so often? No, but the anniversary recalls what was once done and moves us as if we saw the Lord on the cross.
claims: The liturgical remembrance represents the passion without repeating it.

pl-l4d12c5-d1e131.summary: Adds Augustine: Christ was immolated once in himself and yet is immolated daily in the sacrament; once only did he hang on the cross in bodily manifestation, offering himself to the Father as an effective victim for the redemption of the predestined.
claims: Christ hung once on the cross as effective victim.

pl-l4d12c5-d1e139.summary: Quotes Ambrose: the victim powerful for salvation was offered once in Christ. Do we not offer daily? We do, in remembrance of his death, and there is one victim, not many, since Christ was immolated once; this sacrifice is an exemplar of that, and the same is always offered. Offered in many places, it is not many Christs but one Christ, whole here and there; as what is offered everywhere is one body, it is one sacrifice. What we do is a remembrance of the sacrifice, repeated not because of its weakness, since it perfects man, but because of ours, since we sin daily.
claims: There is one victim and one sacrifice, though offered in many places.
The repetition is for our weakness, not the sacrifice's.

pl-l4d12c5-d1e151.summary: Concludes that what is done on the altar is and is called a sacrifice, and that Christ was offered once and is offered daily, but differently then and now; and the power of this sacrament is shown: the remission of venial sins and the perfecting of virtue.
claims: The altar's action is a sacrifice.
The eucharist remits venial sins and perfects virtue.

pl-l4d12c5.summary: Asks whether what the priest does is properly called a sacrifice or immolation, and whether Christ is immolated daily or only once. What the priest offers and consecrates is called a sacrifice and offering because it is a memorial and representation of the true sacrifice on the cross; Christ died and was immolated once in himself, but is immolated daily in the sacrament, where what was done once is recalled. Augustine compares the yearly Easter remembrance; Ambrose says there is one victim, not many, offered everywhere as one body, the sacrifice we offer being a remembrance of his, repeated not for his weakness but for ours. So what is done on the altar is truly a sacrifice; Christ was offered once and is offered daily, but differently; and the sacrament's power is the remission of venial sins and the perfecting of virtue.
claims: What the priest offers is called a sacrifice as memorial and representation of the cross.
Christ was immolated once in himself and is immolated daily in the sacrament.
There is one victim, not many.
The eucharist remits venial sins and perfects virtue.
